title: WHERE DO WE PREPARE FIRST?
detail: One forecast. Thousands of local decisions.
voice: Before a cyclone reaches Bangladesh, one question matters. Where do we prepare first?

title: GHURNI
voice: Meet Ghoorni. From forecast to action. A clearer picture of cyclone wind risk, for Bangladesh.

title: A TRACK IS ONLY THE START.
detail: Which communities? How many people? How uncertain?
voice: A track shows where a cyclone may travel. But which communities face damaging winds? How many people could be exposed? And how uncertain is the answer?

title: KEEP THE UNCERTAINTY.
voice: Ghoorni starts with real archived ensemble forecasts. Each line is one possible storm path. This Remal replay uses forecasts issued before landfall, rather than pretending we already knew the outcome.

title: 72. 48. 24 HOURS.
detail: Compare archived cycles. See what changed.
voice: Compare forecasts around seventy-two, forty-eight, and twenty-four hours before landfall. Watch the estimated impacts change. Ghoorni keeps those changes visible, rather than showing one certain answer.

title: MAKE THE IMPACT LOCAL.
voice: Each member passes through a physics-based wind model. Local boundaries and population estimates connect winds to communities, producing wind-threshold probabilities and a range of possible population exposure.

title: 5,160 UNIONS.
detail: Search a place. Inspect its probability. Compare its forecast cycles.
voice: Explore five thousand, one hundred and sixty unions. Search a place, inspect wind probabilities, and compare forecast cycles. These are estimates of population exposure, not casualty predictions.

title: ACT. PREPARE. MONITOR.
detail: Adjustable rules · explicit thresholds · exportable lists
voice: Adjustable probability rules create Act, Prepare, and Monitor lists. The threshold stays visible, and priorities can be exported. These are planning rules for review, not evacuation instructions.

title: REVIEW BEFORE ACTION.
detail: Template briefing · forecast context · approval step
voice: A template briefing combines forecasts and priorities for human review. Change the forecast or decision rule, and approval resets. Nothing is sent automatically.

title: BANGLA + ENGLISH.
detail: The same map. Two interface languages.
voice: Controls, explanations, and exports work in Bangla and English. The map keeps geography central. Its dated Sentinel-two satellite mosaic provides context, not live storm imagery.

title: TEST. COMPARE. EXPLAIN.
detail: Six historical storms · three lead times · transparent limitations
voice: Evidence compares six historical storms against a single-forecast baseline. Reference impacts use observed tracks and the same wind model. This limited backtest is not independent validation against measured damage.

title: A PROTOTYPE. WITH LIMITS.
detail: Archived forecasts · raw probabilities · estimated exposure
voice: Ghoorni is a historical wind-risk prototype. Numerical forecasts and physical modelling support preparedness analysis. Always follow official Bangladesh Meteorological Department warnings.

title: BUILD TOWARD FIELD USE.
voice: Next: stronger validation and partner feedback. Flood mapping, surge, and shelter access remain planned. Help us evaluate the next steps.

title: BUILT IN BANGLADESH.
detail: International AI Builders Congress · ClimateSphere AI / Climate Shield
voice: Built in Bangladesh by Asim, Tawrat, Fahmida, and Shohidur. We are turning complex forecast information into a clearer starting point for local preparedness.

title: FROM FORECAST TO ACTION.
voice: Ghoorni. From forecast to action. Follow official warnings.
